<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<br class="ltx_break">$ˆ†$Corresponding author: Yi Chang (<span id="id4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">yichang@jlu.edu.cn</span>)</span></span></span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">yichang@jlu.edu.cn</span></a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has demonstrated strong effectiveness in knowledge-intensive tasks by grounding language generation in external evidence. Despite its success, many existing RAG systems are built based on a ranking-centric, asymmetric dependency paradigm, where the generation quality of the generator is highly dependent on reranking results of the reranker.
To overcome this limitation, we reformulate RAG as a cooperative multi-agent decision-making problem and propose Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation (CoRAG), a framework in which the reranker and the generator act as peer decision-makers rather than being connected through an asymmetric dependency pipeline. By jointly optimizing their behaviors toward a shared task objective, the reranker and generator are encouraged to cooperate, ensuring that document reranking and generation work in concert to improve the final response.
Experimental results demonstrate good generalization and improved generation stability of CoRAG, even when the model is trained on only around 10K PopQA samples. Our model released in <a href="https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CoRAG-D63F" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CoRAG-D63F</a></p>
  
</div>
<div id="p1" class="ltx_para ltx_align_bottom">
<p id="p1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center" style="width:345.0pt;"><span id="p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;"></span></p>
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In recent years, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al. (2023b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al. (2024)</a></cite> has emerged as an important paradigm for enhancing the factuality and knowledge coverage of large language models (LLM) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al. (2023b)</a></cite>. A typical RAG system consists of two core components: a retriever and a generator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oche et al. ()</a></cite>. Given a query, the retriever retrieves candidate documents from a large external corpus and further rerank them via reranker.
The generator then conditions on the query and the reranked documents to produce the final response. By explicitly incorporating external knowledge during generation, RAG effectively mitigates hallucinations and achieves strong performance on open-domain question answering tasks<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al. (2024)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18734v1/intro.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:238/118;" width="238" height="118" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span>
Comparison with previous works.
Previous works assume an asymmetric dependency between the reranker and the generator, whereas CoRAG models them as cooperative agents in a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As the reranker plays a critical role in shaping the document context provided to the generator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sharma (2025)</a></cite>, a growing body of recent work has focused on the design and optimization of rerankers and generators <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al. (2023b)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al. (2024)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al. (2025)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shen et al. (2023)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jia et al. (2025)</a></cite>.
However, most existing RAG methods still adopt a ranking-centric, asymmetric-dependency paradigm (Figure 1(a)), where the reranker produces a fixed document ordering and the generator performs generation conditioned on these top-ranked documents. This design tightly couples generation with reranking decisions, making the generator highly sensitive to the reranking results.
As shown in Figure 1(a), if a suboptimal reranker misranks a less relevant document at the top, the generator may produce an incorrect response, even though the optimal document is still present within the top-N set.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">From an optimization perspective, this phenomenon reveals a deeper mismatch between reranking and generation. On the one hand, the generator is highly sensitive to fine-grained ranking results; on the other hand,
learning an exact total order over multiple highly relevant documents is inherently harder than learning a relaxed ordering for the reranker.
For instance, precisely ranking the top three relevant documents as positions 1, 2, and 3 is substantially more challenging than merely ensuring that these documents appear within the top few positions in any order. This discrepancy between the difficulty of ranking optimization and the generator’s sensitivity to reranking results poses significant challenges for the stability and generalization of RAG frameworks in practice.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To address these issues, we reformulate RAG as a cooperative multi-agent decision-making problem, called Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation (CoRAG) (Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>(b)).
Unlike ranking-centric RAG frameworks that enforce a asymmetric dependency from reranking to generation, CoRAG jointly optimizes the reranker and the generator under a shared, task-oriented reward.
This cooperative formulation relaxes the generator’s asymmetric dependency on reranking quality, encouraging the reranker to learn an accurate total order over highly relevant documents and simultaneously training the generator to robustly utilize information rather than relying on a single overly strict ranking.
As a result, CoRAG mitigates the generator’s asymmetric dependency to fine-grained reranking results and improves generation stability.
Experimental results show that, despite being trained on only around 10K PopQA samples, CoRAG significantly outperforms baselines and generalizes well across multiple datasets and tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, this paper makes the following contributions:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We model RAG as a cooperative decision-making problem, treating the reranker and generator as peer agents optimized toward a shared objective.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose a joint optimization scheme that mitigates asymmetric dependency of the generator on ranking results.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Extensive experiments demonstrate improved robustness and generalization of our CoRAG.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Problem Definition</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A typical RAG system consists of two components: a retriever and a generator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lewis et al. (2020)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oche et al. ()</a></cite>.
Given an input query, the retriever retrieves a candidate document set from a large external corpus, which is further refined by a reranker before being used by the generator to generate the final response.
In this work, we focus on the reranker in the retrieval stage together with the generator, as reranking plays a crucial role in improving the relevance and faithfulness of generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sharma (2025)</a></cite>.
We model RAG as a cooperative multi-agent decision-making problem, treating the reranker and the generator as two cooperative agents that jointly determine the final generation outcome, and train them with the goal of maximizing a shared task-oriented objective defined on the generated response.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Specifically, given a query <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and a candidate document set <math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the reranker <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> reranks and selects a set of documents <math id="S2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\subseteq\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\subseteq\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and the generator <math id="S2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> generate an response <math id="S2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}</annotation></semantics></math> conditioned on <math id="S2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>.
The learning objective is defined as</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\max_{\theta,\phi}\;\mathbb{E}_{D\sim\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{D}),\,\hat{a}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\phi}(\cdot\mid q,D)}\left[R(a^{\ast},\hat{a})\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>∼</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{\theta,\phi}\;\mathbb{E}_{D\sim\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(\cdot\mid q,\mathcal{D}),\,\hat{a}\sim\mathcal{G}_{\phi}(\cdot\mid q,D)}\left[R(a^{\ast},\hat{a})\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> are the parameters of the reranker and generator respectively. <math id="S2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(a^{\ast},\hat{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(a^{\ast},\hat{a})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a task-oriented reward defined on the generated response.
This formulation emphasizes that the reranker is optimized not for ranking accuracy, but for its contribution to downstream generation quality. Similarly, the generator is trained to produce outputs that effectively utilize the provided document configuration to maximize the same task-oriented reward.
By aligning both components to the same outcome-oriented objective, the reranker and generator are encouraged to cooperate,
ensuring that document reranking and generation in concert to improve the final response.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An overview of our proposed Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation (CoRAG) is shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.1 The Reranker ‣ 3 Method ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
In the following sections, we first describe the reranker and generator in our CoRAG, and then discuss their joint optimization.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>The Reranker</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The reranker aims to refine the retrieved candidate document set <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> by re-ranking the documents according to their relevance, and selects a subset <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> to provide to the downstream generator for response generation.
Specifically, we obtain <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> in the following steps:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given a query <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and and a document <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in the candidate document set <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}=\{d_{1},d_{2},...,d_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}=\{d_{1},d_{2},...,d_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the relevance score of document <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> by</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}=\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}=\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the reranker and we implemented with BGE-Reranker <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Multi-Granularity, 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We select a subset of top-<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> documents according to the reranker scores and feed them into the generator.</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=\left\{d_{i}\;\middle|\;i\in\operatorname{Top\text{-}K}(\{s_{1},\dots,s_{N}\})\right\}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Top</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=\left\{d_{i}\;\middle|\;i\in\operatorname{Top\text{-}K}(\{s_{1},\dots,s_{N}\})\right\}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18734v1/pipeline.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:215/136;" width="215" height="136" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>CoRAG overview.
The reranker and generator cooperate to generate responses. The task-oriented reward derived from response guides GRPO-aligned training of the reranker and GRPO optimization of the generator.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>The Generator</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Generator is responsible for generating the response <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}</annotation></semantics></math> based on the selected document <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> and the query <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. Specifically, we obtain the predicted response <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}</annotation></semantics></math> with the following steps:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given a query <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and the top-K documents <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>, we input them into the generator model <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> to generate the final response:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}=\mathcal{G}_{\phi}(q,D)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}=\mathcal{G}_{\phi}(q,D),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> is the generator, typically implemented as an autoregressive language model <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Radford et al. (2018)</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al. (2020)</a></cite> that generates the response token by token conditioned on both the query <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> and the document <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>The Optimization</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The reranker and the generator are optimized under a shared task-oriented reward.
From a multi-agent perspective, we treat the reranker and the generator as two cooperative agents with distinct decision roles. The reranker determines which documents to attend to, while the generator decides how to synthesize the final response based on the selected documents. The shared reward, defined on the final response, couples their behaviors and enables coordinated optimization toward task-oriented success.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\mathrm{R}(a^{\ast},\hat{a})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\mathrm{R}(a^{\ast},\hat{a}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{R}(a^{\ast},\hat{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{R}(a^{\ast},\hat{a})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes a task-oriented evaluation function, which we implement to return 1 if the generated response <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}</annotation></semantics></math> contains the ground-truth response <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>a</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math>, and 0 otherwise.
In the following, we detail the optimization of the reranker and the generator under this shared task-oriented reward.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reranker Optimization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike standard learning-to-rank settings <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Casalegno (2022)</a></cite>, document-level supervision is not directly available.
To address that, we transform task-oriented rewards into document-level stochastic preference signals for reranker optimization. Since these signals indicate how documents collectively contribute to task success, we optimize the reranker in a group-relative preference aligned with GRPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shao et al. (2024)</a></cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">First, to transform delayed task-level rewards into document-level stochastic preference signal,
for each document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> in the top-K document set <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> at training iteration <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we assign a binary success signal <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l^{(t)}(q,d_{i})\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l^{(t)}(q,d_{i})\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating whether the generated response achieved task success when <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> was included.
Although this signal provides only a coarse and noisy approximation of individual document contribution under multi-document conditioning, it enables scalable credit assignment without requiring explicit supervision.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Based on these signals,we estimate the expected task success associated with each document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{l}(q,d_{i})=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}l^{(t)}(q,d_{i})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mrow><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{l}(q,d_{i})=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}l^{(t)}(q,d_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the number of historical iterations. To account for uncertainty, we map <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{l}(q,d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{l}(q,d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> to a smoothed Bernoulli parameter</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(q,d_{i})=\alpha+(1-2\alpha)\cdot\bar{l}(q,d_{i})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>l</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(q,d_{i})=\alpha+(1-2\alpha)\cdot\bar{l}(q,d_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in(0,0.5)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in(0,0.5)</annotation></semantics></math>, and we sample a stochastic preference label by:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}\sim\text{Bernoulli}\left(p(q,d_{i})\right),\quad p_{i}\in\{0,1\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mtext>Bernoulli</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}\sim\text{Bernoulli}\left(p(q,d_{i})\right),\quad p_{i}\in\{0,1\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.3" class="ltx_p">This stochastic preference label serves as a surrogate feedback signal for reranker optimization,
enabling us to optimize the reranker in a group-relative preference framework aligned with GRPO.
To conduct the optimization,
we model the reranker as a deterministic scoring function <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> that induces a distribution over candidate documents: <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}(d_{i}\mid q,\mathcal{D})\propto\exp(\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}(d_{i}\mid q,\mathcal{D})\propto\exp(\mathcal{S}_{\theta}(q,d_{i}))</annotation></semantics></math>.
The group-relative advantage <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{A}(q,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{A}(q,d)</annotation></semantics></math> is derived from these preference labels: positive labels (<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}=1</annotation></semantics></math>) indicate relative advantage for document <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> within the group, while a negative label indicates a disadvantage. This leads to the GRPO objective:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}^{r}=-\mathbb{E}_{d_{i}\sim\pi_{\theta}}\left[\hat{A}(q,d_{i})\log\pi_{\theta}(d_{i}\mid q,\mathcal{D})\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>GRPO</mi><mi>r</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}^{r}=-\mathbb{E}_{d_{i}\sim\pi_{\theta}}\left[\hat{A}(q,d_{i})\log\pi_{\theta}(d_{i}\mid q,\mathcal{D})\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">However, directly optimizing the stochastic objective suffers from high variance under noisy credit estimates.
We therefore reinterpret the group-relative advantages as inducing pairwise preferences among candidate documents: documents with higher empirical success rates (more likely to receive positive labels) should be ranked higher. This allows us to reduce GRPO to a deterministic learning-to-rank problem. Constructing positive and negative sets <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}^{-}</annotation></semantics></math> from the sampled labels, we adopt a margin-based pairwise ranking surrogate:</p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rank}}=\sum_{d_{i}^{+}\in\mathcal{D}^{+}}\sum_{d_{j}^{-}\in\mathcal{D}^{-}}\max\!\left(0,\;s_{\theta}(q,d_{j}^{-})-s_{\theta}(q,d_{i}^{+})+\gamma\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>rank</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.808em;" width="1.808em"><mi>max</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rank}}=\sum_{d_{i}^{+}\in\mathcal{D}^{+}}\sum_{d_{j}^{-}\in\mathcal{D}^{-}}\max\!\left(0,\;s_{\theta}(q,d_{j}^{-})-s_{\theta}(q,d_{i}^{+})+\gamma\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is the margin hyperparameter. Although this reduction is not a strict equivalence to GRPO, the ranking loss preserves the group-relative preferences induced by the stochastic labeling scheme and the underlying GRPO objective in expectation. It thus provides a stable and efficient surrogate for optimizing the reranker while maintaining alignment with task-oriented rewards.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Generator Optimization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The generator defines a conditional generation policy
<math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(\hat{a}\mid q,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(\hat{a}\mid q,D)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> is the set of top-K documents selected
by the reranker.
The generator is optimized using standard GRPO for conditional text
generation:</p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}=-\mathbb{E}_{\hat{a}\sim\pi_{\phi}}\left[\hat{A}(\hat{a})\log\pi_{\phi}(\hat{a}\mid q,D)\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mtext>gen</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\text{gen}}=-\mathbb{E}_{\hat{a}\sim\pi_{\phi}}\left[\hat{A}(\hat{a})\log\pi_{\phi}(\hat{a}\mid q,D)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the group-relative advantage <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{A}(\hat{a})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>A</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{A}(\hat{a})</annotation></semantics></math> is computed from the
task-oriented reward <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> using a baseline that compares the current response to other responses in the same training batch.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, both the reranker and the generator are optimized with respect to
the same task-oriented reward, enabling them to cooperatively improve retrieval relevance and generation quality.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the performance of CoRAG, and we particularly focus
on the research questions: (i) Is CoRAG more effective than existing methods <span id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(RQ1)</span>?
(ii) How important are the reranker and the generator to overall performance, and is it necessary to jointly optimize them <span id="S4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(RQ2)</span>?
(iii) How does performance vary with the number of documents used <span id="S4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(RQ3)</span>? (iv) Does CoRAG generalize to other tasks <span id="S4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(RQ4)</span>? (v) Does the CoRAG generator produce high-quality outputs as judged by other LLMs <span id="S4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(RQ5)</span>?</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Setting</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Datasets</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate our method on multiple knowledge-intensive benchmarks, following the dataset setup of recent works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>. Specifically, we evaluate on PopQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mallen et al. (2023)</a></cite>, TriviaQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Joshi et al. (2017)</a></cite> , Natural Questions (NQ) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwiatkowski et al. (2019)</a></cite>, ASQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stelmakh et al. (2022)</a></cite>. Additionally, we include 2WikiMultiHopQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ho et al. (2020)</a></cite>, a Wikipedia-based cross-document multi-hop QA dataset that requires models to reason across multiple documents to derive responses.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation Metrics.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following InstructRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>,
We report correctness, citation precision, and citation recall <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al. (2023a)</a></cite> for ASQA. For the other datasets, we use accuracy measures whether the ground-truth responses are included in the generated outputs.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">

</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following InstructRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>,
We compare our CoRAG with three groups of method: Baselines without Retrieval (relying solely on parametric knowledge, including ChatGPT, Llama-3-Instruct<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{8\text{B}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>B</mtext></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{8\text{B}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and Llama-3-Instruct<math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{70\text{B}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>70</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>B</mtext></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{70\text{B}}</annotation></semantics></math>), RAG without Training (leveraging retrieved documents via in-context learning or prompting, such as In-Context RALM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ram et al. (2023)</a></cite>, Few-shot Demonstration with Instruction, and InstructRAG-ICL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>), and RAG with Training (involving explicit training in the retrieval-augmented framework, including Self-RAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al. (2024)</a></cite> for iterative improvement via self-retrieval, RetRobust <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yoran et al. (2023)</a></cite> for noise robustness training, and InstructRAG-FT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite> for instruction-following fine-tuning with retrieval).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Implementation Details</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt BGE-reranker-v2-m3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Multi-Granularity (2024)</a></cite> as the reranker and Llama-3-Instruct-8B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubey et al. (2024)</a></cite> as the generator. During training,
we use LLaMA3 to provide coarse annotations for positive and negative documents in the training dataset, which helps the reranker learn more effectively by alleviating the sparsity of stochastic preference labels at the early stages of training.
We set the learning rate of reranker to 5e-5, and the learning rate of generator to 1e-5. Both reranker and generator adopt the LoRA fine-tuning strategy for efficient parameter updating. we set <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=1</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq.(<a href="#S3.E10" title="In Reranker Optimization. ‣ 3.3 The Optimization ‣ 3 Method ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>), and the top-K selected documents <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=1</annotation></semantics></math> to precisely attribute the impact of individual documents on task success. During inference, we set <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=3</annotation></semantics></math> for PopQA, TriviaQA, NQ and ASQA, and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=7</annotation></semantics></math> for 2WikiMultiHopQA.
The generator uses a temperature coefficient of 0.7 to balance generation diversity and stability.
It is worth noting that our CoRAG are trained only on PopQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mallen et al. (2023)</a></cite>, while all other datasets are used solely for evaluation, both due to our limited computational resources and to enable assessment of the generalization ability of our CoRAG.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Main Results (RQ1)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The results are reported in Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ Evaluation Metrics. ‣ 4.1 Experimental Setting ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. As it is shown, our method (CoRAG) achieves outstanding performance.
Notably, unlike the InstructRAG
series of methods that perform separate training on each dataset, our model is trained only on the PopQA.
Even so, our method yields state-of-the-art results on four core tasks (PopQA, TriviaQA, NQ and 2WikiMultiHopQA), with the corresponding accuracy rates reaching 71.2%, 81.0%, 72.4% and 58.2% respectively, which significantly outperform existing methods such as RetRobust and InstructRAG-FT. This can be attributed to the joint optimization framework, in which the reranker progressively selects more relevant documents and the generator continuously improves its ability to extract and integrate information from them.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">However, our CoRAG underperforms on the ASQA dataset. We attribute this primarily to the task discrepancy: ASQA requires synthesizing answers from multiple sources and handling ambiguous questions, which differs substantially from the factoid-style, single-answer questions prevalent in our training data (PopQA). Consequently, the retrieval-generator synergy optimized on factoid QA does not generalize effectively to this more complex, multi-answer setting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Ablation Study (RQ2)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To investigate the importance of the reranker and the generator to overall performance, as well as whether it is necessary to jointly optimize them, we conduct ablation studies.
Specifically, we have four variants:</p>
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Rtrain</span>: only finetune the reranker with the labels annotated by Llama-3-Instruct-8B.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gtrain</span>: only finetune the generator with GRPO.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">RGReplace</span>: Replace the generator of CoRAG with Llama-3-Instruct-8B, and replace the reranker with BGE-Reranker in inference.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">GReplace</span>: Replace the the generator of CoRAG with Llama-3-Instruct-8B in inference.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The result presented in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study (RQ2) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>
, we can observe that:
(1) The individually trained RTrain and GTrain underperform CoRAG across both the PopQA and NQ datasets, which implies that a multi-agent cooperative optimization formulation may better capture the interaction between the reranker and the generator, leading to improved performance compared to independent optimization.
(2) Comparing RGReplace, GReplace and CoRAG reveals that the generator contributes more significantly to performance improvement, whereas the reranker plays a relatively limited role. We attribute this phenomenon to the joint optimization. Because the reranker and generator are jointly optimized, the generator may achieve strong performance even under suboptimal reranking signals, potentially weakening the learning pressure on the reranker and reflecting a trade-off in the current design.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To examine this hypothesis, we conduct cross-component experiments by swapping rerankers and generators between CoRAG and other RAG frameworks (Self-RAG and InstructRAG). As shown in Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study (RQ2) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, replacing the reranker with our reranker while keeping other generators (self-RAG and InstructRAG) fixed yields only marginal improvements and occasionally leads to performance degradation. This suggests that the standalone effectiveness of our reranker is relatively limited.
However, when paired with our generator, CoRAG consistently outperforms the variant that combines our generator with BGE-reranker. This contrast reveals an inherent tension between reranking effectiveness and generator sensitivity: jointly optimizing the reranker and generator encourages the generator to rely less on fine-grained ranking signals, which in turn limits the observable gains from further improving the reranker in isolation. Nevertheless, the strong performance of CoRAG indicates that its reranker and generator are well aligned and mutually reinforcing when optimized together.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T3" class="ltx_table">

<table id="S4.T4.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S4.T4.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S4.T4.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">Metric</td>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Top-N Analysis (RQ3)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To analyze how the number of documents provided to the generator affects performance, we evaluate top-1(T1), top-3(T3), and top-5(T5) settings across different datasets. The results are presented in Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study (RQ2) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, which reveal three insights: (1) CoRAG outperforms InstructRAG and RetRobust under all document count settings on both datasets, this indicates that CoRAG can effectively utilize the effective information of documents under different document number; (2) on PopQA, InstructRAG’s performance declines as document number increases (e.g., dropping from 66.19% at T3 to 64.83% at T5), implying more documents may trigger the noise of less relevent documents, and leading to hallucinations.
In contrast, our CoRAG demonstrates a consistent upward trend in performance on both PopQA and NQ, showing strong robustness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Cross-Task Evaluation (RQ4)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To further explore the cross-domain generalization capability of CoRAG, we conduct additional experiments on other tasks, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>. Specifically, we evaluate the generator of our CoRAG and other generator (Llama3 and IntructRAG) on
code generation datasets HumanEval, HumanEval+ <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen (2021)</a></cite>, and table question answering dataset WikiTable Questions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pasupat and Liang (2015)</a></cite>. Results are summarized in Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study (RQ2) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in the table Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Study (RQ2) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, compared with the Llama3 and InstructRAG,
our generator achieves the best or second-best performance across all tasks: on HumanEval and HumanEval+, CoRAG achieves the strongest results on pass@10 and achieves the best pass@1 performance on the more challenging HumanEval+, indicating improved generation quality and robustness on code generation. On WTQ, a table-based question answering benchmark, the generator of CoRAG achieves competitive accuracy, closely matching the strongest baseline while substantially outperforming Llama3. Overall, these results demonstrate that the generator of CoRAG remains effective across both code generation and table-based reasoning tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.6 </span>Evaluation with LLM-as-a-judge (RQ5)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following InstructRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite>, We use LLMs as a judgment to further evaluate the generation of our CoRAG. Specifically, for a given question and documents ranked by reranker, responses are generated by generator and its quality is assessed using different LLMs. The specific prompt template is shown in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Prompt Template ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>. We choose Llama, GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen as the judge. For LlaMa, we use version Llama-3.1-8b-instruction. For GPT, we use version gpt-4o. For DeepSeek, we use version deepseek-v3.2. For Qwen, we use version qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruction. The results are presented in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.6 Evaluation with LLM-as-a-judge (RQ5) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> .
As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.6 Evaluation with LLM-as-a-judge (RQ5) ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation as a Cooperative Decision-Making Problem" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>, CoRAG consistently outperforms both InstructRAG and RetRobust across all evaluation settings, regardless of the LLM used as the judge. CoRAG achieves the highest scores under every evaluator, including pattern-based metrics as well as Llama, GPT, DeepSeek, and Qwen, indicating robust and consistently preferred generation quality.
Notably, the performance gap is most pronounced under the Llama judge, where CoRAG receives higher scores than other LLMs. We attribute this effect to the fact that CoRAG is fine-tuned from Llama, which may lead to a higher alignment between CoRAG’s outputs and the Llama-based judge.</p>
</div>

<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">RAG enhances LLMs’ performance by fusing external documents and is the mainstream solution for knowledge-intensive tasks. Existing research could be categorized into three types based on core efficiency-enhancing mechanisms <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2023b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
The first category is data-driven methods, focusing on the mining and reconstruction of information at the query or document level: Decomposition Prompting <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khot et al. (2022)</a></cite>, which splits complex tasks through prompt engineering. EviNoteRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al. (2025)</a></cite> annotates uncertain information in documents with a note-taking-first approach. HtmlRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tan et al. (2025)</a></cite> uses HTML instead of plain text to preserve semantic structural information.
The second category is model-driven methods, which improve a model’s ability to interpret, filter and utilize retrieved documents through fine-tuning. Representative works include: RetRobust <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yoran et al. (2023)</a></cite> enhances robustness through contrastive training with positive and negative samples. InstructRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wei et al. (2024)</a></cite> explicitly learns the denoising process through self synthesized reasoning. DynamicRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al. (2025)</a></cite> optimizes the order and quantity of documents used to train the reranker through generator feedback.
The third category is strategy-driven methods, also called agentic RAG, which introduces agentic behaviors to dynamically adjust retrieval and generation strategies.
FLARE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al. (2023)</a></cite> triggers lookahead retrieval when encountering uncertain tokens during generation.
SelfRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Asai et al. (2024)</a></cite> introduces a reflection module to synchronously and dynamically adjust both retrieval and generation.
MA-RAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nguyen et al. (2025)</a></cite> decomposes workflows into sub-agents via CoT. ComposeRAG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al. (2025)</a></cite> enables modular agent composition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">From a high-level perspective, CoRAG could be considered similar to agentic RAG, as it models the reranker and generator as cooperative agents. However, unlike many existing agentic RAG methods that treat the retriever (reranker) and generator as separate, modular agents often requiring separate training or intricate prompting for collaboration, CoRAG frames them as a unified policy, eliminating the need for handcrafted coordination mechanisms and allows both modules to adaptively specialize in a task-aware manner.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion and Limitations</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we reformulate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) as a cooperative multi-agent decision-making problem and propose Cooperative Retrieval-Augmented Generation (CoRAG). Unlike conventional RAG frameworks, where the generator exhibits an asymmetric dependency on the reranker and generation quality is highly sensitive to the reranking results, CoRAG treats the reranker and generator as two peer decision-makers. Specifically, the reranker decides which documents, and in what organization, to present to the generator, while the generator determines how to effectively utilize the provided information to accomplish the generation task. Through this cooperative formulation, CoRAG alleviates the generator’s reliance on overly strict document ordering and enables more robust coordination between retrieval and generation, leading to improved overall performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although modeling RAG as a cooperative multi-agent framework improves robustness by reducing the generator’s sensitivity to reranking results, this design may also attenuate the impact of further reranker improvements on generation quality. This reflects an inherent tension between reranking effectiveness and generation sensitivity under joint optimization, which we leave for future exploration.</p>
</div>
</section>
